name: Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL
tagline: Microsoft's managed Citus service for sharded Postgres, now retiring in favor of Elastic Clusters.
description: Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is Microsoft's managed service for Citus, the extension that shards PostgreSQL tables across a coordinator and worker nodes. It began as Hyperscale (Citus) under Azure Database for PostgreSQL and was rebranded under the Cosmos DB umbrella in 2022, despite having nothing in common with Cosmos DB's NoSQL engine. It suited multi-tenant SaaS and real-time analytics that outgrew one Postgres server. Microsoft has since put the service on a retirement path: it is no longer recommended for new projects, and Postgres users are directed to Elastic Clusters in Azure Database for PostgreSQL, which provide the same Citus sharding inside the mainstream Postgres service.
statusNote: Microsoft lists it as on a retirement path and not recommended for new projects; use Elastic Clusters in Azure Database for PostgreSQL instead.

pricing.notes: Billed per node vCore and storage; single-node clusters from a few dollars per day; not recommended for new deployments.

scale.notes: Distributed tables across worker nodes with shard rebalancing; HA standbys and cross-region read replicas.

strengths: Fully managed Citus with built-in PgBouncer, HA and backups
Start on one node and distribute tables later without changing databases
Tracks new PostgreSQL majors quickly because Citus is an extension
weaknesses: On a retirement path; no future for new projects
Confusing branding: unrelated to Cosmos DB's NoSQL APIs
Cross-shard queries on non-distribution columns can be slow
useCases: Existing deployments planning migration to Elastic Clusters
